text.p: Traders attention continued to eye the fortunes of the London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc three months delivery price during brisk and volatile trading on Tuesday.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index was 0.62 points higher at 241.80.

Zinc was thrown into a frenzy after an expected rush towards an upside target of $1,700 a tonne failed in early trading. This prompted investment fund selling which plunged prices to a low of $1,370. At the close of LME afternoon kerb trading zinc stood at $1,480, well down on Monday's seven year high of $1,674 and close of $1,671.
Elsewhere, late afternoon business saw nickel streak ahead as it broke above expected resistance which in turn sparked buy-stops and speculative interest. Last business was at $7,495, up on $7,290.
Copper moved higher after being earlier depressed by another LME stocks rise. It was last at $2,359, against $2,353. Traders were expecting a period of consolidation on Wednesday.
Aluminium again tested resistance above $1,700 on the back of consumer interest and forward buying. It was last at $1,704, up on $1,674.
Lead was quiet and last at $635, down $2, while tin settled at $5,410, up $10. Alloy was quoted at $1,515/20, little moved.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on rallies in the corn and soybean pits, traders said. Some independent strength in wheat may have come from the export sector with Pakistan a buyer of U.S. wheat and European traders Tuesday said Jordan was expected in the market during August for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat. Pakistan bought 500,000 tonnes of white wheat -- 200,000 from the U.S., 250,000 from Australia and 50,000 from Canada, according to the Pakistani embassy in Washington D.C. CBOT soft red winter wheat closed 1/2 to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with September up 1/2 at $3.58 a bushel. December closed 3-1/2 higher at $3.74.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly lower Tuesday, giving back Monday's gains, on good volume, with the exception of palladium which saw new contract highs on NYMEX. COMEX December gold, now the active contract, ended down $3.60 an ounce at $329.80, after trading a $333.40-$329.10 range. Total estimated volume in COMEX gold was 80,000 lots, after 84,734 lots were traded Monday, one of the highest volume days this year. In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $325.70/30, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $326.55 and the New York close Monday at $328.50/00.

IPE Brent ended firmer on Tuesday, drawing strength from a bounding U.S. market which lurched higher again amid expectations that weekly stocks data will reveal a tightening supply situation. September Brent closed 18 cents higher at $18.59 a barrel, failing to match the pace of August unleaded gasoline futures which closed 1.5 cents a gallon higher ahead of the contract expiry on Thursday.
